quiz.q: Emulsifying wax cost ₦9,000 for 500 g. What is the cost of 12 g?
A jar costs ₦2,000 to make. What price gives a 40% margin?
Why is the ingredient cost of a cream much lower than its full cost?
options: Packaging, labour, energy and testing make up most of the cost
quiz.explain: In the worked example, ingredients were about ₦170 per jar but the full cost was about ₦1,540.

quiz.q: A customer asks Rukayat if her body cream will lighten skin. What should she say?
options: No, it is a moisturiser that keeps skin soft
Only if used twice a day
quiz.explain: Honest cosmetic claims describe moisturising and softening. Lightening claims are false for this product.

quiz.q: Which packaging best reduces contamination for a thin body lotion?
quiz.explain: A pump keeps fingers out of the product, which reduces germs entering during use.

quiz.q: Ifeoma's lotion has passed 8 weeks of stability tests. What is the best next step in her plan?
options: Continue to 12 weeks and use small labelled samples for feedback
Remove the preservative to save money
quiz.explain: Sales should be paced by evidence: finish the planned tests and gather feedback before scaling.

finalQuiz.q: Which product always needs a broad-spectrum preservative?
options: A blend of jojoba and baobab oil
A lotion made with distilled water and shea butter
finalQuiz.explain: Any product with water can grow bacteria, yeast and mould, so it needs a broad-spectrum preservative.

finalQuiz.q: What is the job of an emulsifying wax in a cream?
options: To hold oil droplets evenly in water so they do not separate
finalQuiz.explain: The emulsifier sits between oil and water and keeps them mixed as a stable emulsion.

finalQuiz.q: Ada has 99% isopropyl alcohol. About how much does she need to make 200 ml of roughly 70% sanitiser?
options: About 141 ml, topped up to 200 ml with distilled water
finalQuiz.explain: 200 × 70 ÷ 99 is about 141 ml of 99% alcohol, made up to 200 ml with distilled water.

finalQuiz.q: In the heat-and-hold method, what temperature and time are used for the water phase?
finalQuiz.explain: The water phase is heated to around 75°C and held for about 20 minutes; the oil phase is heated to a similar temperature.

finalQuiz.q: A formula has 6% emulsifying wax. How many grams are needed for a 750 g batch?
When should Liquid Germall Plus be added to a cream?
options: In the cool-down phase, below its 50°C limit
finalQuiz.explain: It tolerates heat only up to 50°C, so it goes in once the cream has cooled.

finalQuiz.q: Efe wants a facial oil that lasts well on a warm shelf. Which change helps most?
options: Build the blend on jojoba, add vitamin E and use an amber glass bottle
finalQuiz.explain: A stable base, an antioxidant and light protection all slow rancidity.

finalQuiz.q: Toyin's cream reads pH 6.4 but her preservative works best below 5.5. What should she do?
options: Add a whole spoon of citric acid at once
Add a few drops of citric acid solution, mix, re-measure, and repeat
finalQuiz.explain: Adjust pH gradually in small steps, measuring each time, until the cream is inside the preservative's range.

finalQuiz.q: In a stability test, which sample often shows problems first?
options: The warm sample at about 40 to 45°C
finalQuiz.explain: Heat speeds up separation and other failures, so the warm sample gives the earliest warning.

finalQuiz.q: Which ingredient list order is correct for a cream?
options: By weight, largest first, using INCI names
finalQuiz.explain: INCI names in descending order of weight is the standard way to list cosmetic ingredients.

finalQuiz.q: Which document does NAFDAC's cosmetics registration guideline list among its requirements?
finalQuiz.explain: The guideline lists a laboratory certificate of analysis along with business, trademark, inspection and label documents.

finalQuiz.q: A 50 g jar costs ₦1,540 in total. What price gives a 40% margin?
finalQuiz.explain: 1,540 ÷ 0.6 is about ₦2,567, which can be rounded to ₦2,600.

capstone.title: Natural Skincare Product Development Project
capstone.brief: Produce one emulsified cream or lotion (and, optionally, one facial oil) as a finished product, with a percentage formula converted to grams, a batch record, pH and stability evidence, personal use and feedback notes, an honest INCI label, a costing sheet and a 90-day plan.
steps: Write your formula in percentages, check it totals 100 and convert it to grams for two batch sizes.
Make a final batch using the heat, hold, blend and cool method and complete a batch record.
Measure and record pH and confirm it is inside your preservative's range.
Run a three-temperature stability test for at least 8 weeks and record results with photos.
Use the product yourself and gather feedback from at least one other adult after a patch test.
Design an INCI label with directions and warnings, and cost the product at your chosen margin.
Write a half-page reflection and a dated 90-day plan.
evidence: Formula sheet with percentages and gram columns
Data sheets for emulsifier and preservative with key facts highlighted
Batch record with temperatures, weights and pH
Stability log with photos at each check date
Label draft with INCI list, warnings and directions
Reflection and 90-day plan with at least five dated steps
